beats.label: S1 · Betrayed by Walker
beats.text: Frank is denied the Secretary of State job he was promised; he and Claire decide to destroy the Walker White House from inside Congress.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the grievance that motivates every scheme across the series.

beats.label: S1 · Zoe and Russo recruited
beats.text: Frank blackmails wayward Congressman Peter Russo into total loyalty and turns young reporter Zoe Barnes into his private conduit to the press.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The two people Frank must later murder are introduced here as his tools.

beats.label: S1 · Kern destroyed, Durant installed
beats.text: Frank rewrites the education bill on his own terms and torpedoes Michael Kern's confirmation via Zoe, installing his ally Catherine Durant at State.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Durant becomes a fixture of Frank's cabinet for the rest of the series.

beats.label: S1 · Russo groomed for governor
beats.text: Frank cleans Russo up and runs him for Governor of Pennsylvania, staking the campaign on a Claire-drafted environmental bill.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up the trap Frank will spring to open the vice presidency.

beats.label: S1 · Russo murdered
beats.text: Claire tanks the bill in a private trade with lobbyist Remy Danton; Frank has Rachel Posner wreck Russo on live radio, then kills him with car exhaust.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The first murder — every later investigation traces back to this cover-up.

beats.label: S1 · Frank offered the vice presidency
beats.text: Frank plays President Walker and billionaire Raymond Tusk against each other over Russo's empty seat, and Walker offers him the vice presidency.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The promotion that positions Frank one step from the office he wants.

beats.label: S1 · Reporters close in
beats.text: Zoe, Lucas Goodwin and Janine Skorsky piece together Russo's buried DUI, Rachel's identity and Doug Stamper's role in covering it up.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's hanging thread — the investigation Frank must silence next.

cliffhanger.text: Frank has the vice presidency he schemed for, but three journalists are one step from proving he had Congressman Russo killed.
questions: Can Zoe, Lucas and Janine break the Russo story before Frank silences them?
What does Frank now owe Raymond Tusk, the billionaire who quietly approved his rise?
How long can Doug keep Rachel hidden now that reporters have her name?

characters.name: Frank Underwood
characters.line: House Majority Whip and incoming Vice President; had Russo murdered to open the office.

characters.name: Claire Underwood
characters.line: Frank's wife, runs the Clean Water Initiative; equal partner in every scheme.

characters.name: Doug Stamper
characters.line: Frank's chief of staff and fixer, currently managing Rachel Posner.

characters.name: Zoe Barnes
characters.line: Young Washington Herald reporter; Frank's press mouthpiece and lover, now suspects him of murder.

characters.name: Peter Russo
characters.line: Dead: Pennsylvania congressman Frank groomed for governor and then killed.

characters.name: Rachel Posner
characters.line: Sex worker who witnessed Russo's DUI; hidden and controlled by Doug.

characters.name: Raymond Tusk
characters.line: Missouri billionaire and President Walker's true confidant; Frank's real rival for influence.

characters.name: Lucas Goodwin
characters.line: Herald editor and Zoe's lover, now co-investigating Russo's death.

characters.name: Janine Skorsky
characters.line: Slugline reporter, third leg of the investigation into Frank.

characters.name: Garrett Walker
characters.line: President who betrayed Frank on the Secretary of State appointment.

beats.label: S2 · Zoe silenced
beats.text: The day he is confirmed as Vice President, Frank pushes Zoe under a Metro train; Janine abandons the investigation but Lucas will not stop.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes Frank's most dangerous investigator and sets Lucas on the path to prison.

beats.label: S2 · Frank isolates Walker
beats.text: As Vice President Frank sabotages trade talks with China to weaken Raymond Tusk's grip on Walker, and installs loyal Jackie Sharp as House Whip.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Begins the long campaign to peel Walker away from Tusk; introduces Jackie as Frank's lieutenant.

beats.label: S2 · Lucas framed and jailed
beats.text: An FBI hacker sting frames Lucas for cyberterrorism; he is buried in prison and his warnings about Frank are dismissed as delusion.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Neutralises the last of Zoe's investigators; Lucas returns much later carrying this grievance.

beats.label: S2 · Doug loses Rachel
beats.text: Doug tries to relocate Rachel again; she panics, beats him unconscious in the woods and vanishes with a new identity.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Puts Doug on the sidelines and leaves Rachel as a hanging witness for the next season.

beats.label: S2 · China casino scandal
beats.text: Frank exposes Tusk and Xander Feng laundering Chinese money into GOP attack ads; a special prosecutor is appointed to investigate the White House.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The engineered scandal that will bring Walker down and hand Frank the presidency.

beats.label: S2 · Walker resigns, Frank ascends
beats.text: Frank flips Tusk against Walker, drives the impeachment vote himself, and is sworn in as the 46th President while Doug lies missing in the woods.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The whole series pivots here — Frank has the office he was born wanting.

cliffhanger.text: Frank is the 46th President without a single vote cast for him; Doug lies badly injured in the woods and Rachel is somewhere on the run.
questions: Will Doug survive Rachel's attack, and will he ever find her again?
How does Frank govern a presidency he took by coup rather than election?
Can Lucas Goodwin ever get his story about Frank out from prison?

characters.name: Frank Underwood
characters.line: Sworn in as the 46th President of the United States.

characters.name: Claire Underwood
characters.line: First Lady, complicit in every kill Frank makes.

characters.name: Doug Stamper
characters.line: Frank's chief of staff, last seen beaten unconscious in the woods by Rachel.

characters.name: Rachel Posner
characters.line: Fled Doug after nearly killing him; on the run under a new identity.

characters.name: Jackie Sharp
characters.line: House Majority Whip and Frank's loyal ally in Congress.

characters.name: Remy Danton
characters.line: Former Tusk lobbyist who quietly negotiated with Frank as Tusk fell.

characters.name: Seth Grayson
characters.line: Opportunistic press secretary who defected from Remy to become Frank's man.

characters.name: Cathy Durant
characters.line: Secretary of State, Frank's earliest loyal cabinet installation.

characters.name: Edward Meechum
characters.line: The Underwoods' Secret Service bodyguard and occasional lover to both.

beats.label: S3 · AmWorks launched
beats.text: Frank launches his AmWorks jobs program and lies to Democratic leaders that he will not run in 2016 in exchange for their support.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The program whose failure will define Frank's fight for legitimacy this season.

beats.label: S3 · Claire at the UN
beats.text: Frank pushes Claire into a recess appointment as UN Ambassador after the Senate humiliates her in her confirmation hearing.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Puts Claire on the world stage where Petrov can eventually destroy her.

beats.label: S3 · Dunbar challenges
beats.text: Former special prosecutor Heather Dunbar launches a primary challenge; a relapsed Doug pretends to defect to her camp to spy for Frank.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up the primary race that will pressure Frank for the rest of the season.

beats.label: S3 · Petrov humiliates Claire
beats.text: Claire's Jordan Valley peacekeeping deal with Viktor Petrov collapses when jailed activist Michael Corrigan hangs himself in her cell.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The public humiliation that begins the fracture between Frank and Claire.

beats.label: S3 · Yates and the marriage
beats.text: Frank hires novelist Tom Yates to write his biography; instead Yates draws Claire's private doubts about the marriage into the open.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the man who will become Claire's confidant and lover.

beats.label: S3 · Rachel finally killed
beats.text: Doug tracks Rachel down in the desert, then turns back and buries her, closing Frank's last surviving witness from Russo's murder.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes a permanent liability and cements Doug's ruined obsession.

beats.label: S3 · Claire walks out
beats.text: After Frank tells Claire she is nothing without him, she informs him the next morning she is leaving on the eve of the New Hampshire primary.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The break the next season will spend its opening episodes trying to undo.

cliffhanger.text: Frank has just won the Iowa caucuses, but Claire has walked out of the marriage that built his power.
questions: Where does Claire go now that she is no longer half of the Underwood project?
Can Frank hold off Dunbar's primary challenge without Claire beside him?
What happens to Doug now that he has finally closed the Rachel loose end?

characters.name: Frank Underwood
characters.line: President fighting for the 2016 nomination; marriage collapsing.

characters.name: Claire Underwood
characters.line: Resigned as UN Ambassador; has just left Frank on the eve of New Hampshire.

characters.name: Doug Stamper
characters.line: Back as Frank's chief of staff after hunting and killing Rachel.

characters.name: Heather Dunbar
characters.line: Former special prosecutor now running the primary challenge against Frank.

characters.name: Tom Yates
characters.line: Frank's official biographer, closer to Claire than to Frank.

characters.name: Viktor Petrov
characters.line: Russian president who humiliated Claire and forced her out of the UN role.

characters.name: Jackie Sharp
characters.line: House Whip who dropped out of the race and endorsed Dunbar.

characters.name: Remy Danton
characters.line: Resigned as chief of staff, sleeping with Jackie, leaving politics.

characters.name: Cathy Durant
characters.line: Secretary of State, still Frank's cabinet ally.

characters.name: Seth Grayson
characters.line: Frank's press secretary, jockeying against Doug for influence.

beats.label: S4 · Claire in exile
beats.text: Claire hides at her mother's home in Texas and hires strategist LeAnn Harvey to launch a private congressional bid against Frank's wishes.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces LeAnn, who becomes the Underwoods' key operative for two seasons.

beats.label: S4 · Claire forces the ticket
beats.text: Claire leaks a photo of Frank's father with a Klansman to lose him South Carolina, forcing him to accept her as his running mate.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Restructures the marriage as a formal political partnership for the campaign.

beats.label: S4 · Frank shot at a rally
beats.text: Newly-released Lucas Goodwin shoots Frank at a rally; bodyguard Meechum kills Lucas and dies too, and Frank clings to life awaiting a liver.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes Meechum, brings Lucas's story to an end and hands Claire real power.

beats.label: S4 · Claire runs the country
beats.text: As Frank recovers, Claire quietly walks Vice President Blythe through a Russia crisis, effectively running the White House herself.
beats.whyLoadBearing: First time Claire holds executive power; foreshadows her taking it for real.

beats.label: S4 · Conway's data advantage
beats.text: Republican nominee Will Conway builds a huge polling lead using illegal data mining through the search engine Pollyhop.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces Conway and the algorithmic edge the Underwoods must break to survive.

beats.label: S4 · Underwood ticket confirmed
beats.text: At a brokered Democratic convention Claire out-manoeuvres Cathy Durant, and the Underwoods take the ticket for President and Vice President together.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Puts Claire one election from the office and sours Durant against them.

beats.label: S4 · Total war on television
beats.text: ICO executes hostage James Miller live on video; the Underwoods watch, turn to the camera, and commit to running on national terror.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The campaign strategy for the next season is set here — fear as policy.

cliffhanger.text: The Underwoods have chosen to run on live terror; ICO has just executed a hostage on video and Tom Hammerschmidt has begun tracing Frank's earliest murders.
questions: How far will Frank and Claire go to weaponise fear against Conway's lead?
Will Hammerschmidt's investigation break in print before the election?
Can Doug and LeAnn hold the campaign together while everyone around them cracks?

characters.name: Frank Underwood
characters.line: President and Democratic nominee, recovered from being shot.

characters.name: Claire Underwood
characters.line: His running mate for Vice President, having strong-armed her way onto the ticket.

characters.name: Doug Stamper
characters.line: Chief of staff, secured Frank's stolen liver transplant.

characters.name: LeAnn Harvey
characters.line: Claire's fixer and strategist, now running the Underwood campaign operation.

characters.name: Will Conway
characters.line: Republican nominee and former New York Governor; charismatic war hero.

characters.name: Hannah Conway
characters.line: Will's wife and campaign partner, controls much of the family image.

characters.name: Tom Hammerschmidt
characters.line: Zoe's former editor at the Herald, now investigating Frank's earliest crimes.

characters.name: Cathy Durant
characters.line: Secretary of State; lost her bid for the VP slot at the convention and now resents Frank.

characters.name: Tom Yates
characters.line: Back on staff, quietly resuming his affair with Claire.

characters.name: Seth Grayson
characters.line: Press secretary, walking a line between Frank, Claire and Doug.

beats.label: S5 · Manufactured war on ICO
beats.text: Frank commandeers Congress demanding war on ICO, then secretly executes wanted terrorist Josh Masterson to keep the crisis on the boil.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Terror is now the Underwoods' governing tool, not just a campaign strategy.

beats.label: S5 · Election broken
beats.text: Frank engineers polling shutdowns in Tennessee and Ohio on Election Day; no candidate wins and the vote goes to the House.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Every plot for the next stretch of the season flows from this contested vote.

beats.label: S5 · Claire made Acting President
beats.text: The Senate elects Claire vice president, so she assumes the presidency herself while the House deadlocks between Frank and Conway.
beats.whyLoadBearing: First time Claire actually holds the office — the taste that drives her later choice.

beats.label: S5 · Ohio revote stolen
beats.text: The Underwoods stage a radioactive-truck threat to crack the Conway ticket, force a revote and win Ohio, delivering Frank his second inauguration.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Frank finally has a mandate and a full term to spend on his real endgame.

beats.label: S5 · Committee closes in
beats.text: Congressman Alex Romero reopens the war-declaration probe; Cathy Durant and even former President Walker prepare to testify against Frank.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The investigation that will drive Frank to murder witnesses and eventually resign.

beats.label: S5 · Witnesses removed
beats.text: Frank shoves Durant down a stairwell to stop her testimony; Claire poisons Tom Yates in bed to bury her murder confessions in his manuscript.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Two killings that leave Durant and Yates as loose ends in the next season.

beats.label: S5 · Frank resigns, Claire betrays him
beats.text: Frank stages his resignation planning to rule from outside through Claire's pardon; sworn in, she rejects his call and keeps the presidency for herself.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The final rupture of the Underwood partnership; sets up the next season's power vacuum.

cliffhanger.text: Claire is President and Frank is out in the cold expecting a pardon that is not coming; she is planning a war in Syria alone.
questions: What does Frank do with a presidency he can no longer control from inside?
Can Doug protect Frank's legacy now that Claire has cut him out too?
How much of what Hammerschmidt was chasing will now catch up with Claire?

characters.name: Claire Underwood
characters.line: President; has just cut Frank out and taken the office for herself.

characters.name: Frank Underwood
characters.line: Former President, expelled from the White House and expecting a pardon that isn't coming.

characters.name: Doug Stamper
characters.line: Chief of staff who publicly confessed to Zoe's murder to shield Frank.

characters.name: Mark Usher
characters.line: Conway's former campaign manager who defected to the Underwoods and served as Vice President.

characters.name: Jane Davis
characters.line: Deputy Commerce Secretary and mysterious back-channel operator around Claire.

characters.name: Cathy Durant
characters.line: Hospitalised after Frank shoved her down a stairwell to stop her testifying.

characters.name: Tom Hammerschmidt
characters.line: Reporter closing in on the Underwoods with a mysterious inside source.

characters.name: Tom Yates
characters.line: Dead: poisoned by Claire to bury her murder confessions in his manuscript.

characters.name: Seth Grayson
characters.line: Press secretary, replaced by Claire in her final purge.

beats.label: S6 · Claire alone
beats.text: One hundred days in, Claire is fighting Frank's old billionaire backers, siblings Bill and Annette Shepherd; a sniper's warning shot makes her suspect Frank was murdered.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the season's antagonists and the mystery of Frank's death in one stroke.

beats.label: S6 · Doug institutionalised
beats.text: Doug is in a psychiatric facility claiming he killed Zoe Barnes, unaware that his therapist is quietly reporting to Claire.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Positions Doug as an unstable rival Claire must eventually confront.

beats.label: S6 · All-female cabinet
beats.text: Claire pre-empts a 25th Amendment coup by sacking her entire cabinet and replacing them with women loyal only to her.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The move that consolidates her hold on the office against the Shepherds.

beats.label: S6 · Loose ends murdered
beats.text: In quick succession Cathy Durant, Tom Hammerschmidt and Jane Davis are all killed, silencing the last outside witnesses to the Underwoods.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Every investigator that could still touch Claire is erased.

beats.label: S6 · Frank's heir
beats.text: Claire reveals she is pregnant by Frank, meaning the child — not Doug — will inherit everything Frank left behind.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Redefines the inheritance war between Claire and Doug that drives the finale.

beats.label: S6 · Doug's confession
beats.text: Doug releases Frank's tapes cutting Claire out of the will, then confronts her in the Oval Office and admits he killed Frank to protect his legacy.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Resolves the offscreen death of Frank and sets the final confrontation.

beats.label: S6 · Claire kills Doug
beats.text: When Doug stabs Claire with a letter opener and hesitates, she wrenches it out, drives it into him and suffocates him on the Oval Office floor.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The series' closing image — Claire alone with the office and everyone else dead.

cliffhanger.text: Claire has killed Doug alone in the Oval Office while carrying Frank's unborn heir; every outside witness to the Underwoods is dead.
questions: What becomes of the child who now stands to inherit Frank Underwood's fortune?
Who else knows Claire killed Frank's oldest friend inside the White House?
Can the Shepherds still bring Claire down now that Doug is gone?

characters.name: Claire Underwood
characters.line: President, pregnant with Frank's child, has just killed Doug.

characters.name: Frank Underwood
characters.line: Dead before the season opens; his mysterious death is what Claire spent the season chasing.

characters.name: Doug Stamper
characters.line: Dead: killed Frank to protect his legacy, then killed by Claire in the Oval Office.

characters.name: Bill Shepherd
characters.line: Billionaire industrialist and Frank's old backer, now Claire's chief adversary.

characters.name: Annette Shepherd
characters.line: Bill's sister and Claire's childhood friend, allied against her.

characters.name: Duncan Shepherd
characters.line: Annette's son; discovered he was adopted and was arrested by the FBI for treason.

characters.name: Mark Usher
characters.line: Former Vice President; plotted Claire's assassination with Annette.

characters.name: Seth Grayson
characters.line: Now working for the Shepherd Freedom Foundation against Claire.

characters.name: Janine Skorsky
characters.line: Reporter brought back by Hammerschmidt to keep the investigation into the Underwoods alive.
